notes_context:
Memory items from past tasks:
- [rb-0002] Read the money module before implementing money math: Inspecting ledgerly/money.py and existing invoice functions (line_total, invoice_total) reveals the required helpers and conventions.
  When adding a money-related function, first read the money module and sibling functions to learn available helpers (to_money, round_money, ZERO) and the established pattern of converting inputs then rounding outputs.
- [rb-0003] Handle empty/zero-denominator cases explicitly: Guard against division by zero by returning the module's ZERO constant when total quantity is zero.
  Compute the denominator first and return ZERO (the project's zero-money constant) when it is zero, rather than relying on exception handling or returning a plain int 0.
- [rb-0001] Round money with the project's round_money helper: Monetary results must be rounded via ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent), not Python's round() or bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding.
  Before returning any computed money value, wrap it in the repository's round_money helper. Check ledgerly/money.py for the canonical rounding function and reuse it so invoice totals match finance expectations.

item.title: Mirror sibling-module validation patterns
item.description: Before implementing a new function, grep sibling modules for existing error codes and validation idioms and reuse them.
item.content: Search the package for BillingError raises and isinstance checks to learn the project's conventions (e.g. rejecting bool before int, using to_money/round_money for amounts). Matching those patterns makes hidden tests pass and keeps behavior consistent.

item.title: Read the target test file and models first
item.description: Inspect the dedicated test file, dataclasses, and error class before writing code so signatures and field names match exactly.
item.content: Check models.py for the exact LineItem/Invoice fields and status values, and tests/test_*.py for expected error codes and return values. This avoids guessing attribute names or status strings.

item.title: Guard bools when validating integers
item.description: Python treats bool as an int subclass, so explicitly reject bool before isinstance(x, int) checks.
item.content: When validating a positive integer parameter, write `isinstance(x, bool) or not isinstance(x, int) or x <= 0` to raise the invalid-input error. Also normalize money inputs through the project's to_money/round_money helpers before comparing to ZERO.
